docs.title: Star Org Labs
docs.text:
Run your Star Citizen org like a pro — from Discord to a full web command center. Events, fleet, loot, mining, and org ops in one connected system.

Open the app → Get started

docs.title: Why Star Org Labs?
docs.text:
Running an org is a second job — scheduling ops, chasing signups, tracking who actually showed, splitting loot fairly, keeping the fleet and treasury straight. Star Org Labs pulls all of it into one connected system so you spend less time on spreadsheets and more time flying.

  • Events & Operations

Plan an op in minutes with a guided event wizard. Members sign up for roles and ships in Discord, you reuse templates for regular runs, track attendance & reliability over time, and settle the haul with the built-in Loot Hub.

Events & Ops · Loot Hub

  • Fleet & Hangar

Every member gets a Personal Hangar to register their ships, and leadership gets an Org Fleet Dashboard to see exactly what the org can field — with privacy controls that stay in the member's hands.

Fleet & Hangar

  • Org Command

A home base for leadership: member & server dashboards, personnel roster, org structure, a recruitment hub, support tickets, goals, guild points, treasury, and a public website CMS.

Org Command

  • Industrial

Tools for the working fleet: mining sessions, a cargo optimizer, the RSIG decoder, a rock calculator, and work orders.

Industrial

  • Make it yours

Theme the whole portal to your manufacturer of choice — Aegis, Drake, Origin, RSI, MISC, and more — or set an org-wide look for your members.

  • Lives in Discord

Signups, reminders, and pings happen right where your members already are — plus join-to-create voice channels for the ops nobody scheduled. Your leadership commands from the web; your members never leave chat.

Discord Commands · Voice Channels

docs.title: Ready to launch?
docs.text:
Getting started takes a few minutes and zero installs — sign in with Discord, add the bot, set up your org, and run your first op.

docs.title: Discord Commands
docs.text:
Star Org Labs lives right in your server. Type / in any channel and Discord shows you the bot's commands — but you'll rarely need to memorize them. Most of the action happens through buttons on the event posts. This page is your cheat sheet for when you do want to type.

Who can run what

  • Everyone — no badge.
  • Officer — event and loot organizers.
  • Admin — server owners / configuration.

Officer and Admin are set up by your server's leadership in Server Settings. Servers using Advanced permissions can also grant or restrict whole modules per rank — see Roles & Permissions. A member whose rank lacks a module still sees its commands; running one answers privately that their rank doesn't have access.

Commands run inside a server, with three exceptions that only ever touch your own account and work in a DM with the bot too: /timezone, /boosts, and the /rsi group.

docs.title: 🎮 Joining the action
docs.text:
Everything you need to show up and fly.

Command What it does /events See every upcoming op in your org. /event <id> Open a specific event — with buttons to sign up, pick a role, and choose your ship. /join_event <id> Jump straight into an event. /bring_ship <id> Sign up and bring one of your ships to the fight. /rsi verify <handle> Link and verify your RSI handle so your org knows who you are in the 'verse. /timezone <zone> Set your timezone (e.g. America/New_York) so event times show correctly for you. /templates Browse the templates your org launches ops from — 🌐 global, 🏠 this server.

You mostly just click

Once an event is posted, signing up, choosing a role, and picking a ship all happen with buttons and menus right on the event. /events is usually all you need to type.

docs.title: Your RSI accounts — /rsi
docs.text:
You can link more than one RSI handle (e.g. a main and an alt) and pick which is your main.

Command What it does /rsi verify <handle> Link and verify an RSI handle to your profile. /rsi list See every RSI handle you've linked. /rsi set_main <handle> Choose which linked handle is your main. /rsi unlink <handle> Remove a linked handle.

Renamed: /rsi set_main was /rsi set-main up to and including 1.0.0-beta.196. If it doesn't autocomplete, type the underscore version — every other command on the bot is snake_case, and this was the odd one out.

These four work in a DM with the bot as well as in a server: they only ever touch your own account.

docs.title: 🚀 Your fleet & mates
docs.text: Command What it does /fleet status See your fleet and your mates. /fleet add_mate <member> Add someone as a mate in your fleet. /fleet remove_mate <member> Remove a mate.

docs.title: ⛏️ Mining & industry
docs.text:
Available when your server has Mining Tools turned on.

Command What it does /mining start Kick off a mining session for this channel (officers) — the bot posts a thread for it; track yields and crew on the web. /mining materials Check current material prices and stats (instability, resistance, and more). /mining rock <signature> [laser_power] Decode an RSIG signature or radar ping — mass, composition, and (with laser power) whether you can crack it.

docs.title: 🎧 Star Comms voice ops (beta)
docs.text:
Available when your server has linked its Star Comms shard (Server Settings → External) and is in the Star Comms beta. Every answer is private to you.

Command What it does /comms status Is the operation open, how many are connected, and who is on which net. /comms roster [net] Everyone connected, grouped by net (🎙️ = transmitting). Pick a net to see just that one. /comms assign <member> <net> [minutes] Put someone on a net. Add minutes (1–1440) for a temporary assignment that drops itself (officers). /comms unassign <member> Take someone off their net (officers). /comms open · /comms close Open or close the operation (officers). /comms acars <text> Send an ACARS text (up to 280 characters) to everyone on comms — one a minute (officers). /comms preset list List the presets saved on your shard (saved layouts of who sits on which net) (officers). /comms preset apply <name> Apply a saved preset: everyone in it goes to their net. Applying it twice changes nothing (officers).

Picking a net

Start typing in the net box and the bot lists your shard's nets. Typing part of a name works too — if it matches more than one net, the bot tells you which ones instead of guessing.

Presets

Presets are saved and deleted from the Comms Ops page in the web portal (Presets tab). In Discord, /comms preset apply lists them as you type.

Live updates and channel notices

While your shard is linked, the bot keeps a live copy of who is on comms. /comms status and /comms roster answer from it, and the footer says how fresh it is ("As of 12s ago"). If the live copy is unavailable, they ask the shard directly instead.

An admin can pick a notification channel on the Star Comms card in Server Settings. The bot posts there when someone joins or leaves comms, and when the operation opens or closes. Each kind has its own switch. Push-to-talk is never announced.

docs.title: 🎯 Goals & giving back
docs.text: Command What it does /goal pledge <goal_id> <item> <amount> Contribute materials toward one of your org's goals. /ticket create [category] Open a support ticket with your leadership. /ticket close Close your ticket when it's sorted. /boosts See your Patreon boost slots and the servers you sponsor. /guild boost Spend a boost slot to support this server (raises its capacity). /guild unboost Reclaim a boost slot to use somewhere else.

docs.title: 🎲 Handy extras
docs.text: Command What it does /wheel <names> [mode] Spin a wheel over names you type and pick a winner. mode: Spin to Win or Elimination. /permission Check whether the bot has every permission it needs here, and what's missing.

docs.title: Running ops (Officers)
docs.text:
Organize events, templates, recurring runs, and loot.

EventsRecurring eventsLoot HubSponsorship Command What it does /create_event <template> <title> [date] [time] Launch an op from a saved template. Defaults to today at 20:00 UTC. /delete_event <id> Cancel an event (notifies signups, cleans up channels). The event's signups and attendance are kept, and a server admin can restore it from the web app. /move_event_crew <id> Pull all confirmed attendees into your voice channel. /start_op <id> Ping/DM signed-up members who aren't in voice yet to join your channel. /refresh_event_embed <id> Repost the event to the top of the channel. /create_vcs <id> Create temp voice channels for the event's teams that don't have one yet. /create_template <name> [description] Start a new template, then build it out with buttons. /poll create [title] Post an availability poll. Members vote with the times they can make under Polls on the Fleet Availability page, which the reply links. Needs event-management access. Command What it does /recurring list See your recurring schedules. /recurring create <name> <cron> [days] Auto-post an event on a schedule (e.g. every Friday night). /recurring add_template <id> <template> Attach a template to a schedule. /recurring toggle_roulette <id> Randomize which template runs each time. /recurring toggle_active <id> Pause or resume a schedule. /recurring toggle_poll <id> Let members vote on the next mission — votes weight the roulette, and an officer confirms the winner. /recurring polls See the active mission polls and their vote tallies. /recurring skip_next <id> Take one night off. The schedule keeps running after it. /recurring unskip_next <id> Changed your mind — put that night back on. /recurring one_off <name> <templates> <date> <time> Run a one-off roulette for a single night, with no schedule attached. Command What it does /loot create <name> [event] [points] [sync_vc] Start a loot session. sync_vc adds everyone in your voice channel. /loot roll <session> Run the fair, weighted roll. /loot next_round <session> [points] Move to the next round and top up points. /goal create_template <template> <qty> Set an org goal from a Wikelo preset. /goal create_custom <name> <reward> <reqs> <qty> Create a fully custom org goal. Command What it does

docs.title: Setting up the server (Admins)
docs.text:
Command What it does /setup Quickly create the basic channels and roles the bot needs. Discord shows it to members with Manage Server; if your Admin role doesn't have that permission, grant it the command in Server Settings → Integrations. /settings view Review the current configuration at a glance. /settings set_officer_role <role> Choose which Discord role grants Officer powers. /settings set_admin_role <role> Choose which Discord role grants Admin powers. /settings officers List everyone who currently has Officer powers. /settings set_uex_key Add your UEXCorp API key for live market data (typed into a private pop-up). /ticket category list See the ticket categories members can open tickets under. /ticket category add <name> Add a ticket category (plus optional manager role, auto-close days, and auto-assign role). /ticket category edit <name> Rename a category or change its roles and auto-close days. /ticket category remove <name> Delete a category once it has no tickets left.

Something not working?

If a command doesn't appear, your server may not have that feature enabled, or you may need Officer/Admin. Ask your leadership — or drop into the

Star Org Labs community and we'll help you out.

docs.title: Do I need to install anything?
docs.text: No. Star Org Labs runs in your browser and in Discord. Members never install anything; someone with permission to add a bot to your server adds it once.

docs.title: What does it cost?
docs.text:
Star Org Labs is free to add and free to run your org on. Supporting the project through Patreon is patronage, not a paywall — the cluster costs the same whether you're on it or not.

The commitment we hold ourselves to: nothing that stops you running operations, coordinating your members, or reading your own data gets sold. What support does buy is a longer data-retention window, recognition (a supporters wall, a profile badge), polish on your public org page, and a vote on what gets built next.

Exactly two things scale with supporter tier, and neither is a feature:

Tier-scaled What it means Data retention How long detailed history is kept — 30 days at the free tier, longer with support Boost slots How many servers you can sponsor at once

The public org page, contract scanning, fleet mates and the event and template counts all used to be tier-gated. None of them are now. The public org page is currently early access (off for every org until enabled per server) — that is a rollout switch, not a price.

/boosts shows the slots you have; /guild boost puts one behind this server, and /guild unboost takes it back so you can support somewhere else.

docs.title: Do I have to link my RSI account?
docs.text:
Only if your org asks you to. /rsi verify <handle> links and verifies your Star Citizen handle so your org knows who you are in the 'verse — and it lets the bot sync your org roles from your RSI org page. You can link more than one handle (a main and an alt), set which is your main, and unlink any of them:

/rsi list
/rsi set_main <handle>
/rsi unlink <handle>

Those work in a DM with the bot as well as in a server — they only ever touch your own account.

A handle belongs to whoever proves it. Verifying means pasting the code the bot gives you into your RSI bio, which only the owner of that RSI account can do. If someone else starts verifying your handle, it doesn't block you: the first account to put the code in the bio gets the handle, and anyone else's unfinished attempt is removed, with a notice to them.

docs.title: Why are event times wrong for me?
docs.text: Set your timezone: /timezone America/New_York. Event times, reminders and availability polls all render in your own zone once you have.

docs.title: A command doesn't show up / says my rank doesn't have access
docs.text:
Three possible reasons, in order of likelihood:

  1. The module is off for your server — e.g. mining commands need Mining Tools enabled.
  2. You're not an officer or admin, and it's an organizer command.
  3. Your server uses Advanced permissions and your rank hasn't been granted that module.

In Discord, a member whose rank lacks a module still sees the command — running it just answers privately that their rank doesn't have access. See Roles & Permissions, and ask your leadership.

docs.title: The bot isn't posting events
docs.text: Check that your events channel is configured (/settings view) and that the bot can actually post there. /permission checks whether the bot has everything it needs in your server and tells you what's missing.

docs.title: Can I use this across several orgs?
docs.text:
Yes. Your account, hangar and profile are yours and follow you between servers; each org has its own roster, settings, ranks and data. Your Member Homepage aggregates events from all of them.

Orgs that fly together can also form an alliance and share ops and threat intel — see Org Command.

docs.title: Who can see my ships?
docs.text: You decide, per org, from the privacy panel on your Personal Hangar — everyone in the org, officers and admins only, or nobody. There's a global switch that hides your hangar everywhere, and you can hide individual ships. Details in Fleet & Hangar.

docs.title: We cancelled an event by mistake
docs.text: It isn't gone. Cancelling is reversible: the event, its signups and its attendance all survive, and you can restore it from the web app. See Events & Ops.

docs.title: Is my event feedback really anonymous?
docs.text: Yes. Feedback rows carry no reference to who submitted them, and timestamps are recorded to the day rather than the second, so a comment can't be matched back to a person. Officers see the aggregate — average rating, count, and the comments.

docs.title: Something's broken, or I have an idea
docs.text: Come and say so in the Star Org Labs community. It's a young product and the fastest way to get something fixed is to tell us it's broken.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: Get your org up and running in a few minutes — no installs, no spreadsheets.

docs.title: 1. Open the app & sign in
docs.text: Head to starorg.tools and sign in with Discord. Star Org Labs uses your Discord account, so there's nothing new to create.

docs.title: 2. Add the bot to your server
docs.text: In the app, use "Add to Server" and pick the Discord server you want to run your org from. You'll need permission to add a bot to that server.

docs.title: What the bot asks for
docs.text:
The invite requests a specific, scoped set of Discord permissions — never Administrator. Here's what's granted and why:

Permission Why View Channels See the channels it posts in and manages Manage Channels Create/remove temporary voice channels (voice hubs, event ops channels) Move Members Move members into voice hubs and event voice channels Manage Roles Apply promotions and sync ranks from your RSI org page Send Messages Post event announcements and notifications Send Messages in Threads Reply inside ticket threads Embed Links Rich event and announcement embeds Attach Files Attach generated images (e.g. fleet/roster exports) to messages Read Message History Track poll activity so old polls don't get buried Manage Threads Close and lock resolved ticket threads Create Public Threads Open public ticket and event-discussion threads Create Private Threads Open private ticket threads Manage Events Create, update, and cancel Discord's native scheduled events for your ops Connect Join voice hub channels (required for the bot to grant this to hub owners/members too — Discord only lets a bot hand out a permission it holds itself) Speak / Stream / Priority Speaker / Mute Members / Deafen Members Voice hub owner controls — granted on the owner's own channel only, never server-wide

docs.title: 3. Set up your org
docs.text:
From Server Settings, make it yours:

  • Drop in your org logo
  • Pick a theme — your manufacturer's colors, or a look of your own
  • Configure your channels so events and pings land in the right place
  • Map your officer and admin roles — and see Roles & Permissions for per-rank access control

docs.title: 4. Run your first op
docs.text: Hit Create Event, build out the roster (roles, ships, teams), and share it. Your members sign up straight from Discord — and you track it all from the web. 🎉

docs.title: What's next?
docs.text:
Now that the bot is in, here's where everything lives:

Guide What's in it Events & Ops Planning an op, signups, voice, attendance, the AAR Templates & Recurring Ops Save an op's shape, schedule it, mission roulette Loot Hub Splitting a haul — the four distribution modes and guild points Fleet & Hangar Your ships, who can see them, the Org Fleet Dashboard Voice Channels Join-to-create hubs and the op's own channels Org Command Roster, org chart, promotions, tickets, treasury, goals, CMS Industrial Mining sessions, RSIG decoder, cargo optimizer, work orders

Want the full list of what you can type? See the Discord Commands cheat sheet, or the FAQ for the questions people ask first. Still stuck? Ask in the Star Org Labs community.

docs.title: Roles & Permissions
docs.text: Who can do what in your org — and how to customize it.

docs.title: The basics
docs.text:
Every server starts in Basic mode with three tiers:

Tier Who What they can do Member Everyone in your org Join events, use the loot hub, industry tools, voice tools, track their own career Officer Your event & loot organizers Everything members can, plus the staff surfaces — tickets, treasury, roster, recruitment, attendance, fleet dashboard, org chart, Voice Hubs, a view-only Role Menus page, and a view-only Server Settings Admin Server owners / leadership Everything, including changing Server Settings, building and posting role menus, and the public website CMS. Requesting deletion of the org's data is reserved for the Discord server owner

Officer and Admin are mapped from your Discord roles in Server Settings → Core → Access & Roles. Members with Discord's Manage Server or Administrator permission count automatically.

docs.title: Advanced mode: permissions per rank
docs.text:
Bigger orgs often want more nuance than three tiers — a Logistics rank that can view the treasury, or a probationary rank that can't open loot sessions yet. That's Advanced mode:

  • Every rank in your org chart gets its own set of feature toggles, managed in a matrix on Server Settings → Permissions.
  • Members with no rank have their own pinned row in the matrix, so nobody falls through the cracks.
  • Grants work both ways: you can open staff surfaces (like the treasury view) to a trusted rank, or restrict member surfaces (like events) from one.
  • Management can be delegated too: the Events Management and Loot Management toggles let a rank run recurring schedules, roulette, and loot sessions without making them full officers, and Voice Hub Management opens the Voice Hubs page to a rank.

You can't lock yourself out

Officers and admins always keep their tier's access, whatever the matrix says. Rank toggles only affect regular members — and switching back to Basic instantly restores the classic ladder, keeping your grants saved for later.

docs.title: Turning it on
docs.text: Advanced mode is rolling out gradually. When it's enabled for your server, the switch lives in Server Settings → Core → Access & Roles; flipping it seeds every rank with normal member access, so nothing changes until you start customizing. If the switch tells you it isn't enabled yet, reach out on the support Discord.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• Ranks themselves are created and ordered in Org Chart — the Permissions matrix only decides what each rank can use.
  • Deleting a rank discards its toggles; its members follow the "Unranked members" row until they're re-ranked.
  • In Discord, a member whose rank lacks a module can still see its slash commands — running one just answers privately that their rank doesn't have access.

docs.title: Comms Ops panel (Star Comms beta)
docs.text:
The Comms Ops page shows your org's Star Comms shard live in the web portal: whether the operation is open, which nets exist, and who is on each one. Officers can also run the op from here: assign people to nets, open or close the operation, send ACARS messages, save and apply presets, and set role rules that put everyone with a Discord role on a net.

You'll find it under Events & Ops → Comms Ops. It appears once your server has linked its Star Comms shard (Server Settings → External) and is in the Star Comms beta. The same things are available in Discord through the /comms commands.

docs.title: Running an op on Star Comms
docs.text:
Every event and template has a Voice comms choice: Discord, Star Comms or Both. In the event wizard it is the Voice Comms step after the roster, and on a server with Star Comms linked it is the one place for every voice setting: the Meet Up channel and net, and each team's Discord channel and net (the roster step is just teams and slots). On the full event form and the template form it sits with the voice settings. Star Comms and Both are offered once the shard is linked (below) and your server is in the beta.

  • Discord — voice channels in your server, exactly as before.
  • Star Comms — each team gets a Star Comms net.
  • Both — Discord channels and Star Comms nets side by side.

Pick a Meet Up net for the whole op and a net for each team: one of your shard's existing nets, Create a new net… with a name, or no net. A recurring op or one created from a template gets the template's choice. The event's Discord announcement then shows a Comms section with the Meet Up net and each team's net and a Get Star Comms link and button. The link goes to the download link from the settings card, or the Star Comms website when none is set. On a Star Comms-only op the announcement no longer shows the Discord "Meetup Channel" line — the Comms section's Meet Up → net is where people gather (a Both op shows the two). If the shard is later unlinked, the section quietly disappears and nothing else about the event changes.

Teams and nets can also be changed from the event page: open the op, and in Mission Structure press Manage Nets (Manage Voice on a Both op). A Meet Up net picker for the whole op sits above the teams, and each team has a Team net picker, both with the same choices as the wizard; a Star Comms-only op hides the Discord channel pickers there, and Fleet Command shows each team's net instead of its voice channel. Outside the editor, Mission Structure shows the op's Meet Up → net above the teams.

New nets are created on your shard when the op is saved (it takes a few seconds; "(new)" in the announcement turns into the real net). If the shard is down or refuses — for example a plan that doesn't include creating nets — the op saves anyway and Star Org tries again on the next save and when the op launches. A net Star Org created is removed from the shard when the op ends, is cancelled or is deleted — unless another upcoming op still uses it, which then takes it over — and nets you picked that already existed are never touched. Copying an op gives the copy its own new nets. If the shard is down when an op is deleted outright, its nets stay on the shard.

Putting people on their nets. Everyone signed up to a Star Comms (or Both) op is assigned on your shard to their team's net and the op's Meet Up net — a few seconds after they sign up, swap team or ship, or are moved by an officer, and again whenever a new net is created for the op. Tentative and late signups count; benched, pending and declined ones don't. Members from allied servers are assigned too. Star Comms lets a member sit on several nets, so this only adds nets: someone who was already on a net keeps it, and when they withdraw, change team, or the op ends or is cancelled, Star Org takes back only the nets it gave them — never one they already had or one another upcoming op still gives them. A member the shard doesn't know (not on your Star Comms roster yet) is skipped and everyone else is still assigned; they're picked up on the next change after they join. If the shard is down nothing is lost: the next signup change tries again.

A global template (made by the Star Org team) can carry a Star Comms choice and "create a net" requests, but not your shard's existing nets; a copy into a server without Star Comms falls back to Discord.

docs.title: Linking the shard (server admins)
docs.text:
In Server Settings → External → Star Comms Shard:

  1. Shard URL. Hosted shards live at https://s-<your-org>.star-comms.org — note the s-. The same address without s- is the Star Comms website, not your shard; if you enter it, the card says so and offers the right address in one click. The field is forgiving: a Star Comms launch link, a bare host (s-yourorg.star-comms.org), a host with a port, or an address with a path are all reduced to the shard address, and a short note under the field says what was trimmed. A launch link's id and token are never kept.
  2. Owner API key. Your shard admin creates a scok_… key in the shard's Advanced API Integration settings. The card's Required permissions list shows every scope the key needs, what each one is for, and which are optional (marked for planned features).
  3. Test Connection checks the address is a Star Comms shard and that the key works. Verify permissions checks each scope it can without changing anything on your shard and shows Granted, Missing, Key rejected or Can't check beside it. Write scopes (assigning, ACARS, nets, rules…) can't be checked without making a change, so they show Can't check; make sure the key has them. If every scope says Missing, the key may have none of them — or the shard is refusing this server's IP address. When the shard reports its plan limits (how many nets, whether ACARS is on), they are shown under the list.

Both checks are limited to a few a minute; if you hit the limit the buttons wait until you can try again.

docs.title: What you see
docs.text:
• Four tiles across the top:
    • Operation: open, closed, or unknown (the shard has not said yet).
    • Connected: how many people are on comms.
    • Nets: how many nets the shard reports.
    • Freshness: how current the page is (see below), with how long ago the data was updated.
  • One card per net listing who is on it. A blue badge with a microphone means that person is transmitting right now. People on no net, or on a net the shard no longer lists, appear under Unassigned.
  • The last ACARS message and who sent it.

Names come from your Discord server: the member's server nickname, else their username. Someone who is not a member of your server shows the name the shard has for them, or their Discord ID if it has none. Members who have hidden themselves from the roster are not named.

docs.title: How fresh is it? (about 10 seconds behind)
docs.text:
The page refreshes about every 10 seconds. It does not ask your shard directly. It reads the copy the bot keeps from the shard's live event stream. So when someone joins a net, changes channel or keys their mic, expect the page to catch up within about 10 seconds. That delay is normal, not a fault. Your own changes (an assignment, opening the operation) are sent to the shard straight away; the page shows them on its next refresh.

The Freshness tile tells you how far to trust what you see:

Freshness Meaning Live The bot is connected to the shard and the data is current. Stale The bot has not reported for a few minutes (it may be reconnecting or just starting up). The page shows the last data it has, which may be out of date. Link error The bot cannot reach the shard, or the shard is refusing it (for example a rejected API key). The reason is shown, and the page keeps the last roster it saw. Not set up The server has no working Star Comms link. A server admin sets it up in Server Settings → External.

docs.title: Officer controls
docs.text:
These need the Comms Management permission (officers by default). Members see the panel read-only.

  • Open operation / Close operation. Asks you to confirm first, because everyone on comms sees it.
  • Assign members. Opens a side panel:
    • Choose Assign or Unassign.
    • Pick one or more members. People currently on comms are listed first, then your server's members.
    • For Assign, pick the net. With exactly one member you can also set Temporary (minutes), from 1 to 1440, and the shard removes the assignment when it runs out.
    • Up to 200 members at once. If any net can't be found, nothing is changed.
    • Unassigning several people skips anyone who had no net and tells you how many.
  • ACARS. Type up to 280 characters (the counter shows how many you've used) and choose the alert type: Emergency (the default), Critical or Routine. It is sent to everyone on comms under your server name. Your server can send one ACARS message a minute. After a send, the button shows a countdown until the next one is allowed, and the countdown carries over if you reload the page.

If the shard refuses an action (a rejected key, a missing permission on the key, a rate limit), the panel shows the reason. Nothing is retried automatically, so an action is never sent twice.

docs.title: Presets and role rules (officers)
docs.text: Officers see three tabs at the top of the page: Live (everything above), Presets and Rules. Members only see the live view. Presets and rules are stored on your shard, not by the bot.

docs.title: Presets
docs.text:
A preset is a saved layout: who sits on which net, and whether the operation is open.

  • Save current layout asks for a name and saves the board exactly as the shard has it right now. Saving with the name of an existing preset replaces it (the button says Overwrite preset when it will).
  • Apply shows what the preset will do ("Places 12 members onto Command, Alpha Wing and opens the operation") and asks you to confirm. Members who are not in the preset stay where they are. Applying the same preset twice changes nothing the second time.
  • If a net in the preset has been deleted since it was saved, applying it is refused and nobody is moved. Save the preset again to fix it.
  • Delete removes the preset from the shard. Nobody is moved.

In Discord, /comms preset list shows the presets and /comms preset apply <name> applies one.

docs.title: Role rules
docs.text:
A rule gives a Discord role a net: the shard puts everyone holding that role on it.

  • Each row is a Discord role and a Net. Add rule adds a row; the bin icon removes one. A role can have only one rule.
  • Save rules replaces the whole list on the shard. It does not add to it: any rule you removed from the page is deleted, and the confirmation says how many. Saving an empty list deletes every rule.
  • Only your own server's roles can be used. A rule whose net no longer exists is marked, and must be changed or removed before you can save.
  • Discard changes puts the list back to what the shard has.

docs.title: Events & Ops
docs.text:
Everything that happens between "we should fly Friday" and the after-action report.

An op has four beats: plan it, fill the roster, fly it, close it out. Star Org Labs covers all four — you plan from the web, your members sign up in Discord, and attendance and loot settle themselves.

docs.title: 1. Plan the op
docs.text:
Open Events & Ops → Events and create an event. You get a guided wizard that walks you through the mission, and a drag-and-drop board if you'd rather shape the roster by hand — same event, two ways of building it.

The wizard is five steps in both Basic and Advanced: the basics (game, template, title, organizer), when and where, the roster, announcements (reminders, ping roles, the announce channel, sharing) and a review with the Discord embed preview. A server with Star Comms linked gets a sixth, voice comms, after the roster. Pings start as the game's own ping roles (or the server default) and follow a game change until you edit them. Advanced only adds depth to the roster step (nested assets); nothing about who gets told, or where, is hidden behind it.

Closing the wizard keeps your work as a draft — one per server, so switching servers never opens another server's half-built op — and Resume draft picks it up. A draft saved before drafts went per server moves to the first server you open the wizard in. Anything you entered counts (pings you changed, reminders, shares, a headcount), and a draft you empty again is dropped. Picking a template fills in its reminders too; clear the template picker (the ✕) to go back to a blank mission and drop the template's locked sharing rows while keeping what you typed. If the save is refused, the reason shows beside Confirm & Schedule rather than in a passing toast. Let Them Vote (roulette mode) is offered on phones as well, and opening a vote no longer throws away the event draft you had resumed: the draft comes back as it was before you switched to the vote.

If you shared the new event with allies, the wizard stays open after Confirm & Schedule and lists each ally: Shared, Excluded with the reason (for example, an alliance invite not yet accepted), or Failed with the reason (for example, no events channel set). Failed allies have a Retry button that sends the announcement to that ally again and updates the line. Close when you are done. An event shared with nobody closes straight away, as before.

Voice comms is where you pick how the op talks: Discord (voice channels in your server, exactly as before), Star Comms, or Both — and it holds every voice setting: the Meet Up channel and net, and each team's Discord channel and net (on that server the roster step is just teams and slots). It appears once your server has linked a Star Comms shard and is in the Star Comms beta; until then the team voice channels stay on the roster step. With Star Comms, the op and each team get a net — pick one of your shard's existing nets or name a new one, created on the shard when you save — and the Discord announcement gains a Comms section listing the nets and a Get Star Comms button. The review step's preview shows that Comms section too, so a misnamed or missing net is caught before you confirm, and a new Meet Up net must be named before you can move on. The same choice is on the full event form and on templates. See Running an op on Star Comms.

An event carries:

  • Groups — the squads or wings people join (Alpha, Escort, Salvage Crew…)
  • Roles — the jobs inside a group (Pilot, Turret, Medic…)
  • Vehicle slots — ships the op needs, which members fill from their Personal Hangar

Prefer Discord? /create_event <template> <title> [date] [time] launches an op from a saved template. Date defaults to today, time to 20:00 UTC.

Build it once, reuse it forever

Almost nobody builds an op from scratch twice. Save the shape as a template and every future run starts pre-filled — see

Templates & Recurring Ops.

docs.title: Where the announcement lands
docs.text: Each event announces to a channel and pings a set of roles. Star Org Labs resolves that in order: the recurring schedule's override, then the template's channel and ping roles, then your server default from Server Settings. So your mining runs can ping @Miners in #industry while your combat ops ping @Combat in #ops, with no per-event fiddling.

docs.title: 2. Fill the roster
docs.text:
The event posts to Discord as an interactive embed. Members click buttons — join, pick a group, pick a role, bring a ship. Nobody has to learn a command.

If you'd rather type What it does /events List every upcoming op this server can see /event <id> Post that op's signup embed with all its buttons /join_event <id> Sign up directly /bring_ship <id> Sign up and commit one of your ships

Ship selection reads straight from your Personal Hangar, so "who's bringing the Reclaimer" answers itself.

Not sure when to fly?

Open Fleet Availability in the sidebar. Every member fills in their usual weekly hours once, and the page turns them into a timezone-aware heatmap of when your org can actually show up, so you schedule around your members instead of guessing.

For a one-off question ("Friday or Saturday?"), an officer can run /poll create. The poll appears under Polls on the same page, and members vote with the times they can make.

docs.title: 3. Fly it
docs.text:
When it's time, the op runs itself as much as possible.

  • Voice channels — the event can create temporary channels for its groups. /create_vcs <id> makes any that are missing, and they're cleaned up when the op ends.
  • Gather the crew — /move_event_crew <id> pulls every confirmed attendee into your current voice channel.
  • Chase the stragglers — /start_op <id> pings and DMs signed-up members who aren't in voice yet.
  • Split and regather — the event's tactical controls on the web split your crew into squad channels and pull them back together for the debrief. They live in Fleet Command, which the event's organizer and anyone with event-management permission can open.
  • Auto-launch — if your attendees are sitting in the meetup channel at start time, the op launches on its own.
  • Repost — /refresh_event_embed <id> puts the event back at the bottom of a busy channel.

docs.title: 4. Close it out
docs.text:
Attendance is automatic. At each lifecycle step — and whenever you regather — the bot scans the event's voice channels and records who was actually there. That includes walk-ins: people who never signed up but flew anyway are credited too, and listed on the report.

The after-action report. When the op ends, the Mission Lead gets a DM asking for an AAR. Fill in the short web form and it posts to your AAR channel with the attendance attached, and is kept for your org's stats.

Anonymous feedback. If your server has event feedback enabled, the finished event shows a Give Feedback button. Participants leave a 1–5 rating and an optional comment, stored with no link back to who wrote it — officers see only the aggregate on the event card. Use it to find out which ops people actually enjoyed.

Attendance stats. Over time, Events & Ops → Attendance turns all of that into reliability: who shows up, who signs up and vanishes, who quietly carries every run.

docs.title: Cancelling — and un-cancelling
docs.text: /delete_event <id> (or the web equivalent) cancels an op. It notifies your signups and tears down the Discord channels, announcement and scheduled event — but it does not throw anything away. The event, its signups and its attendance all survive; it renders struck through with a CANCELLED badge, and you can restore it from the web app if the call was premature.

docs.title: Flying with other orgs
docs.text:
Events can be shared with allied orgs through the Alliance Hub, so a joint op has one roster instead of three. Members of an allied server see the shared event in /events and sign up from their own Discord. Events that belong to another org and were never shared with you stay invisible — an event id from someone else's server simply answers "not found."

When you create an op, the Share with allies section (Announcements step) lets you pick an alliance and send it to all allied servers, which includes servers that join later, or to selected servers only. Allied servers that can't receive it, because their seat has event sharing turned off or they haven't accepted the invite yet, are shown greyed out with the reason. Other servers shares directly with orgs outside your alliances that trust yours. After sharing, you're told which servers missed the post and why, for example "no events channel set".

Next: Templates & Recurring Ops · Loot Hub · Fleet & Hangar

docs.title: Fleet & Hangar
docs.text: Your ships, your org's ships, and who's allowed to see them.

docs.title: Your Personal Hangar
docs.text:
Personal Hangar sits in the sidebar on every page — it's yours, not any one org's. Register the ships you actually own, name them if you like ("Rust Bucket" stays "Rust Bucket", it doesn't get folded into "Cutlass Black ×2"), and they become available everywhere else:

  • Event signups — /bring_ship and the event's ship picker read straight from it
  • Org Fleet Dashboard — your hulls count toward what the org can field
  • Public profile — a shareable page showing your fleet, awards and certifications

docs.title: Importing instead of typing
docs.text: Already tracking your fleet elsewhere? Import FleetView on the Personal Hangar page brings the whole thing in at once, instead of adding forty ships by hand.

docs.title: Privacy — you decide who sees what
docs.text:
The privacy panel on the Personal Hangar page is the member's side of this, and it's layered:

Control Effect Hide my hangar everywhere You disappear from every org's fleet views — officers and admins included — and your public profile's fleet empties. Beats everything below. Per-org visibility For each org you're in: Everyone in org, Officers & admins only (the default), or Hidden Per-ship hidden Individual ships you'd rather not list at all

You always see your own ships, whatever these say. And a hidden hangar isn't advertised as hidden — a private member is simply absent from the roster, not rendered as an empty row.

Server admins have their own switch on top of this: an org can refuse to show its fleet to non-members at all.

docs.title: The Org Fleet Dashboard
docs.text:
Org Management → Org Fleet Dashboard answers the two questions leadership actually asks, from two angles:

  • By Model — "does the org have enough Reclaimers?" Every visible hangar aggregated into one row per ship, with a count and who owns them.
  • By Member — "what does this person bring to an op?" No aggregation; each ship keeps its own identity and custom name.

Opening a member shows their hangar and their recent ops side by side — useful when you're picking a crew and want to know both what they fly and whether they show up.

docs.title: Fleet mates
docs.text:
Some ships need a crew. Mates are the people you habitually fly with, tracked on your own fleet:

Command What it does /fleet status Your fleet and your mates /fleet add_mate <member> Add someone as a mate /fleet remove_mate <member> Remove one

All three answer privately — your fleet isn't channel content.

On the web, the same list lives in Settings → Account & RSI → Mates: add someone by their Discord user ID (turn on Developer Mode in Discord, right-click them, Copy User ID; they must have signed in to the portal once), and remove them with the button on their row.

Each row also says which supporter tier that mate inherits from you. If you back the project at Fleet Commander or Fleet Admiral, your mates get the same tier for as long as they're in your fleet; below that they inherit nothing and the row says so.

No mate cap

Mates used to be limited by Patreon supporter tier, and the limit was zero below the top tier. That gate is gone — add as many mates as you like. See the FAQ.

Next: Events & Ops · Org Command

docs.title: Industrial
docs.text:
Mining, salvage and hauling, with the accounting handled for you.

Everything here lives under Industrial & Economy in the sidebar.

docs.title: Mining sessions
docs.text:
A session is a live lobby for a run. The crew joins from the web, logs what they pull as they pull it, and the payout is computed when you close.

Starting one. An officer runs /mining start in the channel the run belongs to. The bot posts a thread with a join link a moment later, and the session opens on the web.

Running one. Everyone on the crew opens the session and picks a role. From there it's live — yields, expenses and crew changes appear for everybody as they happen, with no refreshing. Scouts push rock scans in, miners log SCU, logistics logs the fuel and the repairs.

Two switches change how a run behaves:

  • Locked — no new participants may join
  • Org run — the takings belong to the org rather than the crew, and pay into the Treasury

Closing one. Closing is the payout. Star Org Labs totals the gross yield, subtracts logged expenses, splits the net by each member's share ratio, and posts a receipt to Discord. There's no separate "pay out" step, and the org-run switch locks the moment you close — by then the crew has been paid on the strength of it.

docs.title: RSIG Decoder
docs.text:
Point it at a scan and it reads the rock for you. Screenshot the in-game scanning UI, paste it into the decoder, and it extracts the signature, works out mass and composition, and tells you whether the rock is worth the trip.

The OCR runs in your browser — the screenshot never leaves your machine.

In Discord, /mining rock <signature> [laser_power] does the same from a signature string: validity, mass, composition, instability, resistance — and with a laser power, whether you can actually crack it.

docs.title: Rock Calculator
docs.text:
The physics sandbox. Build a fleet of mining ships, fit lasers, modules and gadgets, feed it a rock's mass, resistance and instability, and get a crackability verdict with the exact power numbers behind it.

Use it to answer "do we need a second Mole for this?" before you fly out, not after.

docs.title: Cargo Optimizer
docs.text: Hauling contracts, routed properly. Enter your contracts — or screenshot the contract UI and let the in-browser OCR read them — then the optimizer solves the route: which pickups and drop-offs in which order, given your ship's capacity, as a step-by-step flight plan.

docs.title: Work Orders
docs.text:
A job board for the org. Create Order opens a form: give the job a title, an optional description, a category (Mining, Salvage, Hauling, Security, Crafting or Other) and an optional aUEC reward. Members claim it and status tracks through to done. (Opening orders to other orgs is planned; the form does not offer it yet.)

Accept claims an open job and makes you its assignee; after that, the assignee can mark it Complete. Editing the job, reassigning it, reopening or cancelling it, or completing a job someone else holds is for whoever posted it, or an officer — the board only shows Complete to those people. Reopening a job clears its assignee, so anyone can claim it again. The poster or an officer can Cancel an open or in-progress job — it stays on the board under the Cancelled filter. Only an officer can Delete a job outright, after a confirmation, which erases it.

docs.title: Industry Hub & the internal market
docs.text: The Industry Hub is the module's landing surface, and it carries the Internal Org Market: a WTB/WTS classifieds board for your members. List what you're selling, cancel it when it's gone, buy from your own org instead of the trade channels.

docs.title: Prices and market data
docs.text:
Material prices and refinery estimates come from UEXCorp. Admins can add the org's own UEXCorp API key with /settings set_uex_key — typed into a private pop-up, never into a slash-command option, so it doesn't land in Discord's command history.

/mining materials shows current estimated prices and game stats — base signature, instability, resistance, mining type — sorted by value.

Mining Tools is a toggle

/mining materials and /mining rock need Mining Tools enabled for your server. /mining start is officer-only. If a command doesn't appear or answers that your rank lacks access, check with your leadership — see Roles & Permissions.

Next: Org Command · Discord Commands

docs.title: Loot Hub
docs.text:
Split a haul without an argument, a spreadsheet, or a three-hour Discord thread.

A loot session is a live room: the host logs what dropped, participants bid points on what they want, and a weighted roll settles it. Everything mirrors to a Discord thread as it happens.

docs.title: Running a session
docs.text:
Open Events & Ops → Loot Hub, or start one from Discord:

Command What it does /loot create <name> [event] [points] [sync_vc] [admin_only] Open a session. points defaults to 100; sync_vc adds everyone in your current voice channel; admin_only runs it without a seat for you /loot roll <session> Run the weighted roll /loot next_round <session> [points] Next round, and top everyone up

sync_vc is the fast path when the crew is already in voice.

docs.title: Changing a hub after it started
docs.text:
The hub's Admin tab has two cards for an open hub:

  • Hub Settings: change the voice channel, the text channel or the linked event (loot managers only, as when creating). You can also change the payout method until someone has been paid, and switch the distribution mode of every item nobody has won yet. Moving the text channel starts a fresh thread there and reposts the manifest. You can change the point pool: everyone's points move by the difference, so what they already spent or were awarded is kept (raise 100 to 150 and a member on 40 goes to 90). A pool that would leave someone below zero is refused. Loot managers can also switch guild points on or off, but only before anyone has bid, won, been awarded points or been topped up by Next round. Everyone's points then restart from the new source: their guild points, or the point pool.
  • Add Participants: pick members, Add everyone in voice, or Add event attendees once an event is linked. New seats start with the same points as joining yourself. People already in the hub are skipped, and it works on a locked hub.

docs.title: Running a hub without bidding
docs.text:
Tick Run as admin only when you create the hub, or later in Hub Settings. You and your co-hosts are then not seated, can't bid, and are skipped by voice and on-time point awards. Turning it on later removes your seat only if you have no bids, wins or awarded points in the hub. Round top-ups and pool changes don't count, since everyone has them.

In a guild-points hub you can also tick Still credit admins for on-time attendance. The on-time award then adds the same guild points to you and your co-hosts as to everyone else who arrived on time, once per hub, without seating you. Voice awards still skip you. A hub on its own point pool has no lasting points to credit, so the option isn't shown there.

docs.title: What Discord sees
docs.text:
The session gets its own thread, and the thread stays readable:

Message When 💰 Loot Session Started You open the hub ➕ Loot Added Someone logs new loot — names them and what they logged 📦 Loot Manifest The running haul, edited in place so there's one current list, not a scrollback 🎲 Roll Results Every roll ✅ Payout Complete Each participant paid out

If your server never bound a loot channel, the hub still works fully on the web — it just posts nowhere.

Did the announcement post? The hub list and the hub's Hub Settings card show the state of the Loot Session Started post: Posting… while it is on its way, Posted (with Open in Discord) once it is up, or Failed with the reason, for example a missing bot permission or a deleted channel. Fix the cause, then press Repost to try again. A hub with no text channel shows nothing.

docs.title: Payout method
docs.text: New hubs start on Items only (no aUEC tracked): the hub records who won what and leaves the money out. Pick Track aUEC value per item to price each win at the item's aUEC value, or Even split of total aUEC to divide the haul's total value equally. You can change it in Hub Settings until someone has been paid. Hubs created before this default changed keep the method they had.

docs.title: Bidding
docs.text:
Each participant has a point balance for the session. You bid points on the items you want; higher bids mean better odds, not guaranteed wins.

Two rules cut across every mode:

  • A zero bid never rolls. Bid nothing, win nothing.
  • You must be able to afford the roll. If your balance is under what this roll would cost you, you're out of that draw.

Joining as a guest? Your seat belongs to the browser tab you joined from — pick a name nobody in the session is using, and keep bidding from that tab. A name that is already taken can't be claimed by someone else typing it in.

docs.title: The four distribution modes
docs.text:
Every item carries its own mode, so one session can mix a "one each" rule for the rare drop with a free-for-all on the ore.

Mode Who can win How your bid weighs What a win costs Max One anyone who hasn't won it yet your bid your bid Diminishing (default) anyone who can afford it halves with each win you already have your bid the first time, free after Even Split anyone who can afford it your bid divided across the stack the same divided amount Take All anyone who hasn't won it yet your bid your bid, once, for the whole stack

Diminishing is the default, and the safe one: you can win the same item twice, your odds drop each time so the stack spreads around, and repeat wins don't cost you anything.

Even Split treats a bid of 100 on a stack of 4 exactly like bidding 25 four times over.

Take All is for the thing that only makes sense whole — one roll takes the entire stack.

The free-roll rule nobody expects

Under Max One, Diminishing and Even Split, if there's enough to go around, nobody pays. When the number of distinct bidders is at or below the remaining quantity, everyone wins for free. Five bidders on a stack of five all walk away with one and spend nothing.

Take All has its own version: free only when you were the only eligible bidder.

docs.title: Items nobody bid on
docs.text: A session-level switch decides what happens to an item with no eligible bids. Off (the default) leaves it unsettled. On hands it to a random participant, no bid required and no points charged, repeating until the stack clears.

docs.title: Guild Points
docs.text:
A session can run on guild points — your org's persistent currency — instead of throwaway session points. Then a roll isn't just tonight's split: every win writes to the member's point ledger, and showing up regularly is what earns the standing to win the next big drop.

In a guild-points session you can bid up to your current guild points, and a win costs exactly the points you spent — nothing else on your balance changes. Round top-ups from Next round are extra room for that session only; they never add to your guild points. The on-time award pays each member once per session.

Guests cannot join a guild-points session: a bid spends your org's ledger, so you need to sign in as a member of the org. A seat with no guild-points balance in the org never wins an item, by bid or by the unbidded hand-out.

Officers manage the ledger under Org Management → Guild Points.

docs.title: The Quick Wheel
docs.text:
/wheel <names> [mode] spins a wheel and picks a winner — giveaways, "who flies the Idris", settling a tie.

  • Spin to Win — one spin, one winner.
  • Elimination — spin repeatedly, knocking names out until one is left.

Next: Events & Ops · Org Command

docs.title: Org Command
docs.text:
The leadership side: who's in the org, where they sit, how they get promoted, and how the org pays for things.

Everything here lives under Org Management in the sidebar. Most of it is officer or admin territory — see Roles & Permissions for who sees what.

docs.title: Member Homepage & Org Dashboard
docs.text:
Two landing surfaces, aimed at two different people.

Member Homepage is a member's own view — their upcoming events, awards and notifications, across every org they're in. It's always one click away in the sidebar, whatever module you're using.

Org Dashboard is the org's pulse: what's happening in this server right now.

docs.title: Personnel Roster
docs.text: Every member of the org in one list, with their rank, their billet and their history. It's the surface you actually use to run the org day to day — find someone, see what they fly, check whether they've been showing up.

docs.title: Org Chart
docs.text:
Your org's structure, built as units containing billets — the posts people hold. Drag members into billets to assign them; units nest, so a wing can hold squadrons that hold flights.

Ranks are created and ordered here too. In Advanced permissions mode, ranks are also what the permission matrix hangs off, so the order you set here is the order your org actually runs on.

docs.title: Ranks, promotions & awards
docs.text:
Promotion requests. Ranks can carry criteria — time in service, attendance, certifications — and members can request the next step when they meet them. Officers work an approve/deny queue, and an officer can also set a member's rank directly from the roster, which supersedes any request still open for that person. On the Personnel Roster, each member's ⋯ Manage button at the end of their row holds Set Rank, Assign Billet, Issue Award and Grant Certification.

Two switches control the flow: an org-level toggle for whether members may request promotions at all, and per-rank settings for whether a rank can be a promotion target or is hidden from the ladder entirely.

Promotions are a web workflow today

Approving a promotion updates the member's rank in Star Org Labs. It does not currently swap their Discord role or announce anything to a channel — that half is on the roadmap. Your Discord roles stay yours to manage (or to sync from your RSI org page).

Awards & certifications. Define your org's medals and qualifications, issue them to members, and let members pin them to their public profile. Certifications double as promotion criteria.

docs.title: Recruitment Hub
docs.text:
A public apply page for your org and a review queue behind it. Applications land in the queue, officers work them, and accepted members flow into the roster.

The apply page hangs off your org's public website — see the CMS below.

docs.title: Tickets & Support
docs.text:
Support that works from both sides of the wall.

Members open a ticket with /ticket create [category]. It becomes a Discord thread — private or public depending on the category — and replies sync both ways. /ticket close closes it when it's sorted. Only the ticket's author, the category's manager role, or an officer can close one.

Staff work the same cases as a Kanban board under Tickets & Support: statuses, priorities, assignment, and internal notes that the requester never sees.

Categories are yours to define — Recruitment, Griefing Report, Ship Loan, whatever your org actually gets asked. Each can carry a manager role, an auto-assign role and an auto-close window:

Command What it does /ticket category list The categories members can pick from /ticket category add <name> Add one /ticket category edit <name> Rename it, or change its roles and auto-close days /ticket category remove <name> Delete it — once it has no tickets left

A member-facing ticket page is rolling out

My Tickets lets members open and follow their own cases from the web instead of Discord. It's in early access; if you don't see it yet, your server doesn't have it turned on.

docs.title: Org Treasury
docs.text: A virtual bank in aUEC, with a ledger: deposits, withdrawals, taxes and payouts, each with who and why. Industrial sessions marked as org runs pay into it automatically when they close.

docs.title: Goals
docs.text:
Org-wide objectives with material requirements — "we need 4,000 SCU of Quantanium for the next push." Members pledge what they've hauled and progress updates live.

Command What it does /goal pledge <goal_id> <item> <amount> Contribute toward a goal /goal create_template <template> <qty> Create a goal from a Wikelo preset (officer) /goal create_custom <name> <reward> <reqs> <qty> Build one from scratch (officer)

docs.title: Guild Points
docs.text: Your org's own currency and standing. Points accrue through participation and are spent in the Loot Hub when a session runs on guild points — so the people who keep showing up are the people with the weight to win the next big drop. Officers manage the ledger here.

docs.title: Alliance Hub
docs.text:
Orgs don't fly alone. An alliance is a bloc of orgs with an invite-and-accept handshake and its own roles. Once you're in one you get:

  • Shared events — an op posted by one member org can be shared to the others, with a single roster instead of three
  • A shared threat / KOS ledger — intel about hostile orgs and players, pooled across the bloc

Everyone in the org can read the ledgers; the controls that change them stay with staff.

docs.title: Public Website CMS
docs.text:
Every org gets a public page — a slug, hero image, logo, a features list, social links and your theme — plus the apply page that feeds Recruitment. Admins edit it under Public Website CMS; no HTML involved.

Early access

The public page is switched off for every org for now — it is early access, not a paid feature (it used to need Champion-tier support; that is gone for good). The nav entry only appears once it is enabled for your server. To get in, ask in the community Discord.

It's a page, not a marketing site

The public page renders in the browser rather than being pre-rendered on the server, so search engines and link previews see less of it than a visitor does. Fine for "here's our org, here's how to apply" — don't count on it ranking.

Next: Roles & Permissions · Industrial

docs.title: Templates & Recurring Ops
docs.text: Set your weekly ops up once and stop rebuilding them every Friday afternoon.

docs.title: Templates
docs.text:
A template is the shape of an op saved for reuse: its groups, roles, vehicle slots, description — plus where it announces and who it pings.

Find them under Events & Ops → Event Templates, or from Discord:

Command What it does /templates List the templates you can use — 🌐 global, 🏠 your server's /create_template <name> [description] Start a new template, then build it out with buttons /create_event <template> <title> [date] [time] Launch an op from one

The reply to /create_template is private, and only you or an officer can use its builder buttons.

Global templates

Templates marked 🌐 ship with Star Org Labs — common op shapes you can use straight away. Your own 🏠 templates stay private to your server.

docs.title: Announcement routing
docs.text: Each template can carry its own events channel and ping roles. Every way of creating an event honours them — web wizard, bot command, recurring schedule, roulette — falling back to your server default when the template leaves them blank. If you leave Ping Roles untouched, the template pings your server's default roles. Clearing the selection sets the template to announce without pinging anyone, and Use server default switches it back.

docs.title: Voice comms
docs.text:
A template also carries the op's voice comms choice — Discord, Star Comms or both — and, for Star Comms, a Meet Up net and a net per team (an existing one or a new one by name). Every event made from the template, including recurring and roulette runs, gets the same choice; a template only plans new nets — each event creates its own on the shard. A new Meet Up net needs a name: Save stays blocked ("Name the new Meet Up net") until you give it one. See Running an op on Star Comms.

The editor also has a Meet Up channel picker: the voice channel ops from this template muster in before launch. Leave it on Server default to use your server's Meet Up channel.

docs.title: Building a template on the web
docs.text:
• Event shape. In a multi-game server, pick Fleet, Roster or RSVP. An RSVP template has no teams — just going, maybe and can't — so it saves with only a name. Switching a fleet template to RSVP drops its teams when you save. Changing the game or the shape away from Roster also clears the Mythic+ requirement, which only a roster template can hold. The Signups choice (open or curated) sits in the roster section, beside the Mythic+ score.
  • A game your server switched off. A template already tagged with a game, or set to Roster or RSVP, keeps the Game and Event shape pickers even after your server drops to one game, so you can move it to the game you still run or to Shared / no game.
  • Meetup Offset must be filled in: use 0 for no muster period. Clearing it used to save 30 without telling you.
  • Reminders. A new template uses the server's reminder times.
  • Why Save is greyed out, and any reason the server turned the save down, show in the box above the buttons. The server's reason clears once you change something.
  • Live Preview sits beside the form on very wide screens and under it everywhere else. It shows your server's default pings when Ping Roles is untouched, and none when you've cleared it.
  • Nothing is lost by accident. Closing a template you changed asks first. A new template is kept as a draft for this server: Create Template brings it back, and Discard draft clears it. If you switch servers while the editor is open, it closes, so nothing from one server gets saved into another. The draft stays with the server you started it in.
  • Template cards count units by amount: a team with four Prospectors on one line shows 4 units, the same number the event wizard shows.

docs.title: Recurring schedules
docs.text:
A recurring schedule posts an event automatically on a cron schedule. Manage them on the Recurring tab of the Events page, or from Discord:

Command What it does /recurring list Your schedules /recurring create <name> <cron> [days] Create one — e.g. 0 20 * * 5 is Friday 20:00 /recurring add_template <id> <template> Attach a template to a schedule /recurring toggle_active <id> Pause or resume /recurring skip_next <id> Take one night off — the schedule keeps running /recurring unskip_next <id> Changed your mind; put that night back

days is how far in advance the event posts (default 2 days), so members have notice.

A schedule can override the template's announcement channel and ping roles, which means one template can serve several schedules that each shout in a different place.

docs.title: Planning queue
docs.text:
Want Friday to be Siege of Orison, then Tech Smugglers, then whatever wins the vote? Open the Event Planner (Events & Ops in the sidebar, or Open planner on a schedule card) and line the next few weeks up.

  • Pick a schedule at the top. Each row shows the date the op is projected to run on.
  • Upvote the ops you want. Votes are advice for officers, not a draw — tap again to take yours back.
  • Officers can add an op from any template (with a title, description or notes just for that night), drag rows to reorder, pin an op to a specific date, remove it, or hit Sort by votes once to put the most-wanted first. The queue holds up to 26 ops.
  • Each run takes the top of the queue. Once an op is created it shows 🔒 and can no longer be moved or voted on; if the event is cancelled before it starts, the op goes back to the top.
  • Dates you are skipping show as Skipped, and a date that already has a member vote open shows as Voting — the queue leaves both alone.
  • History (collapsed at the bottom) lists what ran, what was cancelled and what was removed.

The queue comes first

While anything is queued, the schedule runs the queue instead of opening a vote or spinning the roulette. Roulette and polls pick again as soon as the queue is empty.

If two people change the queue at once — a drag, an add, a pin, even a vote — the second change is refused and the planner reloads the latest queue, so nobody silently overwrites anyone else. Just redo it.

Everyone sees the "queue comes first" note on the planner when the schedule would otherwise vote or spin. Queued ops that have not been created yet also appear on the org dashboard's calendar as dashed planned entries — click one to open the planner. They turn into normal events once the schedule creates them.

If Trigger now can't create the queued op, you'll see "Nothing was scheduled; try again" — the queue is unchanged, so it's safe to retry.

A schedule can also keep an Upcoming ops board posted in a Discord channel: pick an Upcoming Ops Board Channel when you create or edit the schedule.

docs.title: Mission Roulette
docs.text:
Attach several templates to a schedule, turn roulette on, and each occurrence draws one at random. Nobody knows if Friday is bounty hunting or salvage until it posts.

Command What it does /recurring toggle_roulette <id> Random template per run /recurring toggle_poll <id> Let members vote on the draw /recurring polls Live tallies for open polls /recurring one_off <name> <templates> <date> <time> A one-night roulette with no schedule behind it

docs.title: Letting members vote
docs.text:
With polls on, members vote on the template pool ahead of the run — from the poll board on the Events page or straight from a Discord select menu. Votes weight the draw rather than deciding it: a template with three votes is likelier, not guaranteed. An officer confirms (or overrides) the drawn mission before the event is created, and an auto-confirm fallback handles the nights nobody gets to it.

Keep voting chatter out of your announcements

Roulette polls can post to their own channel, separate from where events announce. If a poll gets buried under newer messages, it can be reposted at the bottom of its channel automatically — off by default, since not every org wants the bump.

Next: Events & Ops · Loot Hub

docs.title: Voice Channels
docs.text: Star Org Labs manages two kinds of voice channel, and they behave differently on purpose.

docs.title: Join-to-create channels (voice hubs)
docs.text:
A hub is a voice channel that makes channels. Join ➕ Create Squad and the bot spawns a fresh channel shaped by that hub's template, moves you into it, hands you the controls, and deletes it once the last person leaves.

These belong to you, not to an op. Use them for the pickup group at 2am that nobody scheduled.

As the owner of a spawned channel you get the usual controls — rename it, lock it, adjust who can join and speak. Renaming has a short cooldown, because Discord rate-limits channel renames and a spammed rename would leave the channel stuck with the wrong name for everyone.

You can also mute, deafen and move people — but only in your own channel: the bot grants those as a permission on that channel, not across the server. One Discord quirk to know: a server mute or deafen stays on the member after they leave your channel, until a moderator lifts it. Unmute people before they head elsewhere.

Leave the hub and come straight back and you're moved into the channel you still own. Once that channel is gone, a new one is ready after 30 seconds — join-and-leave churn would otherwise make and delete a channel every time.

Setting them up

Officers and admins configure hubs and their templates on the Voice Hubs page under Command Staff in the sidebar (orgs on advanced permissions can open it to a rank with the Voice Hub Management toggle). One template can back several hubs, so you describe the shape once — "Squad Channel" — and attach it to ➕ Create Squad and ➕ Create Wing alike, instead of maintaining two copies that slowly drift apart.

Time spent in a hub channel does not count as event attendance. That's deliberate: hanging around in a party channel isn't the same as showing up for the op.

docs.title: Event voice channels
docs.text:
These belong to an op and die with it. The event creates channels for its groups, the bot moves people around during the run, and everything is torn down when the op ends or is cancelled.

Command What it does /create_vcs <id> Create temp channels for any of the event's teams that don't have one /move_event_crew <id> Pull every confirmed attendee into your current voice channel /start_op <id> Ping and DM signed-up members who aren't in voice yet

Time in these channels is attendance — including for walk-ins who never signed up. See Events & Ops.

Give the two systems separate categories

If your voice hubs spawn into the same Discord category your ops use as their rally point, both systems compete for that category's 50-channel limit — and whoever asks for the 51st gets turned away mid-op. The Voice Hubs page warns you when you pick a colliding category. It's a legitimate choice for a small org; it just shouldn't be a surprise.
